task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and an explainer of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about why Alderbank's first electric-bus depot plan has fewer charging points than buses. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Alderbank Transit plan provides six charging points for an initial fleet of 12 electric buses.
The operating plan staggers connections across the buses' return and departure schedules instead of assuming every vehicle must charge at once.
One charging point can serve more than one bus during a planned overnight sequence, but that is not a guarantee under every disruption.
The plan depends on available charging time, the energy needed for assigned work and the site's electrical capacity.
Bus routes return at different times, so the first vehicles back can use points before later vehicles arrive.
The six-point installation is the first phase; spare physical space for more equipment does not mean additional chargers are already funded or operating.
Fleet engineer Orla Marr said, "We are planning a sequence of vehicles, not setting a rule that every bus owns its own plug."
The depot team will assign charging positions and monitor completion as part of the vehicle-ready process before departure.
A bus being physically parked beside a charger is not itself confirmation that it has received the energy needed for its next assignment.
The operator has included contingency arrangements for equipment outages in its internal operations plan, without publishing a promise of uninterrupted service.
Driver representative Tera Cole said, "The first morning will be about more than the batteries. It will be about who has checked which bus is ready."
Drivers and depot staff are receiving training on the new handover records and reporting responsibilities.
The buses have not yet entered regular passenger service, and the packet contains no completed fleet-reliability result.
Commissioning will test the installed equipment and the proposed sequence before the operator publishes the final start arrangements.
The electricity network connection requires its own approval and readiness checks, separate from delivery of the buses.
A delivered bus or installed charging pedestal therefore does not establish that the entire depot system is ready.
The initial routes were selected for their operating patterns and depot access, not announced as a conversion of the whole transit network.
The packet does not supply a measured annual emissions reduction or fuel-cost saving from regular operation.
The old diesel maintenance bays remain in use for vehicles outside the first electric fleet.
The depot's vehicle board will show both the next route assignment and the charging handover status.
Charging points are for the transit fleet and are not being opened as a public car-charging service.
A later expansion will depend on operational findings and a separate funding decision.

forbidden_additions: A charger permanently dedicated to every bus or an already converted entire fleet.
Guaranteed reliability, completed commissioning or measured annual savings.
A ready network connection inferred merely from equipment delivery or public charger access.
preserve: The planned sequence and the dependencies between vehicles, equipment, power and staff handovers.
Planned capacity distinguished from tested operating results.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
